stem.text: The elements in Period 3 and their compounds show trends across the period from sodium to sulfur.

stem.caption: Options A to D
head: electronegativity of the elements
acid–base behaviour of the oxides of the elements

explanation.text: Across Period 3 the nuclear charge increases while the shielding stays about the same and the atomic radius decreases, so the attraction for bonding electrons, i.e. electronegativity, increases from sodium to sulfur.

The oxides change from ionic and basic (Na<sub>2</sub>O, MgO), through amphoteric Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, to covalent and acidic (SiO<sub>2</sub>, P<sub>4</sub>O<sub>10</sub>, SO<sub>2</sub>, SO<sub>3</sub>). This change follows the rise in electronegativity: as the difference in electronegativity from oxygen gets smaller, the bonding becomes more covalent.

optionAnalysis.text: Electronegativity increases across the period, not decreases.
Correct. Electronegativity increases from Na to S, and the oxides go from basic through amphoteric (Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>) to acidic.
Electronegativity is right but the oxide trend is reversed; Na<sub>2</sub>O is basic and SO<sub>3</sub> is acidic.

reasoningChain: Electronegativity: nuclear charge rises, radius falls, shielding similar, so it increases across the period.
Oxides: Na<sub>2</sub>O and MgO basic, Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> amphoteric, SiO<sub>2</sub> to SO<sub>3</sub> acidic.
The row with 'increases' and 'basic → amphoteric → acidic' is C.

inferredMistakes.text: Confusing the electronegativity trend with the atomic radius trend, which decreases across the period.
